summary.text: Primates are an order of mammals split into strepsirrhines, which include lemurs, and haplorhines, which include tarsiers, monkeys and apes.
They have large brains relative to body size and rely more on visual acuity than on smell, which is the dominant sense in most mammals.
Primates are among the most social animals, and about 60% of primate species are threatened with extinction.

facts.label: Smallest primate
facts.value: Madame Berthe's mouse lemur, about 30 g

items.prompt: A biologist says "monkey" is not a proper formal group in modern classification. What is her reason?

options.label: It includes lemurs, which come from a different order
It leaves out hominoids, who share the same common ancestor
It has been replaced by the older term Anthropoidea
It covers only New World species and ignores the rest

items.explain: Monkeys are paraphyletic because the group excludes hominoids, who are also descendants of the common ancestor Simiiformes, and modern classifications name only monophyletic groups.

items.prompt: Most mammals explore the world mainly through one sense. Compared with them, which sense do primates lean on more?

options.label: Sharp vision, at some cost to the sense of smell
Hearing, at some cost to touch
Taste, at some cost to vision
Smell, at some cost to hearing

items.explain: Primates rely more on visual acuity at the expense of smell, which is the dominant sense in most mammals.

items.prompt: Baboons spend most of their time on the ground rather than up in the branches. What is still true of them?

options.label: They have lost every trace of tree-climbing ability
They are no longer counted as primates
They rely on brachiation to travel across open ground
Like every primate species, they have adaptations for climbing trees

items.explain: Some primates are mostly ground-dwelling, but all species have adaptations for climbing trees.

items.prompt: A young primate is compared with a mammal of the same size from another order. What is likely to differ?

options.label: The primate matures sooner and lives longer
The primate matures later and lives a shorter time
The primate matures later and lives longer
The primate matures at the same age but lives longer

items.explain: Primates develop more slowly than similarly sized mammals, reach maturity later and have longer lifespans.

items.prompt: A conservation group wants to protect as many primates as it can. Which action targets the biggest threat?

options.label: Stopping large-scale clearing of tropical forest for agriculture
Ending the hunting of primates for use in medicines
Ending the keeping of primates as pets
Ending the monkey drives that move primates around

items.explain: Large-scale tropical forest clearing for agriculture most threatens primates, although hunting and other pressures also contribute.

items.prompt: A writer says "apes include humans." Is that statement wrong?

options.label: Yes: no scientific source has ever included humans among the apes
Not necessarily: some authors define apes to include humans, and there is no consensus
Yes: ape has always meant exactly the same thing as monkey
No: a 2021 agreement settled that apes always include humans

items.explain: Benton defines apes to include humans, while other sources do not; as of 2021 there is no consensus.
